text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- New regulations governing the construction of buildings in Hanoi have been submitted to the Ministry of Construction for approval. The draft regulations aim to simplify and streamline procedures for approving building plans in the inner city.

-- Laotian Deputy Prime Minister Bounyang Vorachith is expected to arrive in Hanoi on Wednesday for a four-day official visit. He will attend the opening of the 19th meeting of the joint Vietnamese-Laotian governmental commission on cooperation.

-- Banking chiefs have vowed to win back the industry's "lost credibility" this year, raising the amount of capital for long- and medium-term loans and improving its management and training procedures.
-- Half of the foreign brand names in circulation in Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City have been manufactured in Vietnam, a survey by the Ministry of Trade's Market Management Department showed.

-- The Ministry of Trade has announced criteria for businesses to export rice and import fertiliser this year. Those wishing to export rice must have import-export licences, be members of the Vietnam Association for Rice Exporters and must have engaged in exporting rice indirectly or directly for three years prior to the date of application and have earned receipts of at least 50 billion dong ($4.47 million) per year.

-- The United Nations Development Programme and the government are holding a two-day workshop to discuss the legal framework needed to establish and regulate a stock exchange and securities markets in Vietnam.

-- Vietnam will upgrade the infrastructure of three focal economic zones in the north, centre and south of the country and develop axis routes linking the three zones by the year 2000, Acting Minister of Communications and Transport Le Ngoc Hoan said.
-- The World Bank has signed an agreement to lend Vietnam $55 million for the development of roads in rural areas.
-- More than 7,700 narcotics-related cases were uncovered between 1993 and 1996.
-- Vietnam Airlines carried 2.57 million passengers, including over one million foreigners, and 44,000 tonnes of cargo in 1996.
-- Vietnam plans to produce 60,000 tonnes of tea by the year 2000, 40,000 tonnes of which will be for export.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet has urged Mekong Delta provinces to transplant their winter-spring rice crop, which has been delayed by serious flooding during the last crop.
